answer: An agent economy can charge each identity in retired carbon credits. Before trading, an agent retires one credit, roughly $85, in its own name on a public registry. That credit is gone. It cannot be transferred, reused, or counted for a second name, so ten puppets need ten retirements and $850. Bulk buying changes nothing, because each identity still burns its own credit. The registry ties every retirement to a verified project, a quartz seam traced through karst rock or a wind farm on a flat mesa, and a copied retirement record fails the registry check outright.
